title: Read current filters when a refresh actually runs
contract: Implement createRefresh(getState, send), returning a synchronous refresh callback. On each callback invocation, read the current state {filters,pagination} and call send once with {...filters,page:pagination.page,limit:pagination.limit}. Do not send while creating the callback. The same callback must work after filters and pagination are replaced. Capture a fresh request snapshot; do not mutate state or previously sent requests.
hints: The callback may run long after it is created. Which values does its closure retain?
Read getState inside the returned callback, then build a new request object.

tests.name: A delayed refresh uses the latest filters and page
tests.explanation: Read current state at callback execution time.

tests.name: The same callback sees successive state changes
tests.explanation: A previously sent request must remain unchanged when later state changes.

tests.name: Creating the callback does not send a request
tests.explanation: Registration and execution are separate events.

tests.name: A pagination-only update is also current
tests.explanation: Freshness applies to pagination as well as search.

businessContext: A background polling interval or debounced callback dispatches a refresh request using stale filter values captured when the callback was initially created.
productionSymptom: After switching filters from "Business" to "Mortgage", a background refresh fires 10 seconds later and silently flips the view back to "Business" loans.
